entries.title: Jeremiah 48:1
segments: Against Moab; in this prophecy Jeremiah makes a free use of the earlier prophecy of Isaiah.  The reader may consult the notes on

, where will be found an account of many of the places mentioned in this chapter, and also an explanation of many of its peculiar expressions.  The overthrow of Moab, however, which Isaiah predicted, was not the same as that which is here foretold.  The former took place in connection with the captivity of the ten tribes, and in Isaiah's day,

; the latter, as also that of the nations mentioned in the following chapters, was accomplished by Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
  Kiriathaim; in the northern part of Moab, west of Medebah. 
 
The sins of the Moabites which brought upon them God's displeasure were their great pride and arrogance, manifested in trusting to their own defences and treasures, and in maginifying themselves against the Lord,
; also their hatred and contempt of God's people, leading them to help forward and exult over their calamities.
For these sins God made Moab "a derision and a dismaying to all them about him."
Since the principles of God's government are unchangeable, all who follow the example of Moab, whether nations or individuals, must expect to receive punishment at God's hand.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:2
segments: They have devised evil; the enemies of Moab have devised; in allusion to the signification of the word Heshbon, that is, "device," as it is rendered in

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:6
segments: Be like the heath in the wilderness; that is, solitary and desolate.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:7
segments: Chemosh; the national god of the Moabites.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:10
segments: Cursed be he; he among the executioners of God's wrath upon Moab.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:11
segments: Settled on his lees; as the flavor of wine is increased by leaving it to stand on the lees, so long tranquility had increased the strength and riches of Moab, and with these his pride.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:12
segments: Wanderers, that shall cause him ot wander; better, "emptiers, that shall empty him."  The original word means to empty by laying a vessel over on its side.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:13
segments: Of Beth-el; that is, of the golden calf which they worshipped there.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:15
segments: Gone up out of her cities; or, "her cities are gone up," that is, in smoke.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:17
segments: The strong staff--beautiful rod; the sceptre of his power.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:18
segments: Daughter; a metaphor for the inhabitants of Dibon, as "virgin daughter of Babylon," etc.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:19
segments: Aroer; on the northern bank of the Arnon.  Its inhabitants come out to inquire of the fugitives that pass through it in their flight, "What is done?"

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:24
segments: Bozrah; this seems to have been Bozrah in the Hauran, on the border of the Arabian desert, and not the Bozrah which is mentioned in
, as belonging to Edom; the latter lay south-east of the Dead sea.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:26
segments: Make ye him drunken; with the wine-cup of God's wrath.
He also; that is, as well as Israel.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:27
segments:
A derision unto thee; when carried into captivity by the Assyrians. 
 
  Was he found among thieves? that is, was he detected by Moab in such a crime as made him a just object of his derision?  Compare
Spakest of him; of his calamities.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:28
segments: Be like the dove; hide yourselves in dens and caves from the enemy. Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:30
segments: Not be so; as he purposes.  Compare

segments: Kir-heres; the same as Kir-hareseth.

segments:
vv 31-32. 
 
  I wll weep for thee--no shouting; see notes on

  The sea of Jazer; of this nothing further is known. 
 
  Their shouting shall be no shouting; their joyous vintage-shout shall become a battle-shout, shall become a cry of distress.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:34
segments:
From the cry of Heshbon--uttered their voice; the cry of distress which begins at Heshbon extends to Elealeh and Jahaz. 
 
  From Zoar even unto Horonaim; supply, "they have uttered their voice." 
 
  A heifer of three years old; see note on
The waters--of Nimrim shall be desolate; see note on

segments: Like a vessel wherein is no pleasure; compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:40
segments: He shall fly; the conqueror.

entries.title: Jeremiah 48:45
segments:
They that fled; the Moabites who fled before the invading army. 
 
  Stood under the shadow of Heshbon; sought protection within its walls. 
 
  Because of the force; because of the invading force; but many render these words, "without strength." 
 
  A fire--out of Heshbon; the conqueror shall send forth thence his bands to ravage the country. 
 
  Sihon; that is, the city of Sihon; the same as Heshbon.  See the history of this city,
, from which passage this and

are taken. 
 
  The tumultuous ones; the boastful warriors of Moab.
